title: 21.3 A Segmented-Interlacing Multi-Phase Hybrid Converter with Inherently Auto-Balanced ILs and Boosted IL Slew Rate During Load Transients
problem: Multi-phase buck/hybrid converters suffer from inductor current imbalance due to duty-cycle mismatches, requiring per-phase current sensing and closed-loop adjustment. Low inductor slew rate creates large output voltage undershoot during load transients.
motivation: Datacenter point-of-load (PoL) power delivery demands minimized guard bands (undershoot margins) and elimination of complex current-balancing control to reduce power loss and design complexity as computing power scales.
method: Segmented-interlacing multi-phase hybrid converter with inherent auto-balancing via duty-cycle compensation and simultaneous energization of all inductors during load transients to boost slew rate, eliminating per-phase current sensing.
key_novelty: Inherent inductor current auto-balancing without per-phase sensing, achieved through segmented architecture and dual-mode control.
contributions: Auto-balanced inductor current distribution removing per-phase sensing/tuning complexity
Boosted IL slew rate through simultaneous multi-inductor energization
Reduced guard band enabling tighter output voltage regulation
